stem: An exceptional child is referred to as either a child who is a genius academically, manually, or physically, or which OTHER type of child?
options: A child who is exactly average in all domains
A child who has never been assessed
A child who attends only private school

stem: Into how many main classifications is the exceptional child divided?
Children who are exceptionally good or exceptionally up to date physically, manually, and academically are referred to as what?
Children who are exceptionally poor educationally, physically, and manually are referred to as what?
Handicapped children can be further divided into which two groups?
options: Mentally handicapped children and maladjusted children
Physically fit children and physically unfit children

stem: Which of the following conditions is classified under mentally handicapped children?
options: Mongolism, imbecility, moron, and educationally subnormal

stem: According to the definition given, the term 'handicap' refers to which of the following?
options: Any disability of the body, intelligence, or personality which is likely to interfere with the individual's growth and development and, at times, their capacity to learn
A temporary condition that always resolves without intervention
A condition found only in children over the age of 15
A term used exclusively for physical sporting ability

stem: The causes of the exceptional child can be broadly divided into which two categories?
Acquired causes of exceptionality are described as secondary to which of the following?
options: Other conditions such as infections or drugs

stem: Congenital/hereditary causes can be due to congenital aetiological causes or which other type of factor?
options: Environmental factors occurring after age five
Factors related solely to maternal occupation

stem: 'Congenital' causes, as defined in this classification, refer to abnormalities of which structures?
Which condition is listed as resulting from a congenital (genetic/chromosomal) cause?
Which inborn error of metabolism is specifically listed as a congenital cause of exceptionality?
Besides Down syndrome and phenylketonuria, which of the following is ALSO listed as a congenital cause?
options: Microcephaly, muscular dystrophy, and sickle cell

stem: 'Prenatal' causes are described as factors affecting the already formed foetus in utero, especially during which period?
options: The final week before delivery only

stem: Prenatal causes of exceptionality are also referred to by which alternative term?
Thalidomide is given as an example of which type of prenatal cause?
Malaria and German measles are given as examples of which type of prenatal cause?
Besides drugs and infections, which of the following are ALSO listed as prenatal (environmental) causes?
options: Maternal antibodies, maternal toxemia, dietary factors, and radiation
Old age and malnutrition occurring after birth

stem: Acquired aetiological factors are subdivided into which two categories?
Perinatal or natal causes are described as defects due to which of the following?
options: Complications of delivery, which can cause handicap, for example trauma
Abnormalities of the genes and chromosomes
Factors affecting the foetus during the first trimester

stem: Fetal anoxia, as a perinatal cause of handicap, is specifically due to which of the following?
options: Either maternal haemorrhage or cord prolapse
Dietary deficiency in the third trimester only

stem: Besides fetal anoxia and trauma, which of the following are ALSO listed as perinatal/natal causes?
options: Hypoglycemia, respiratory or metabolic acidosis, and birth asphyxia

stem: Postnatal causes of handicap are defined as causes that occur in which time period?
Which infection is specifically listed as a postnatal cause of handicap?
Besides infection and trauma, which of the following are ALSO listed as postnatal causes of handicap?
options: Poisoning, electrolyte imbalance, malnutrition, and radiation
Chromosomal abnormalities and inborn errors of metabolism

stem: Prevention of handicap is organized into which three levels?
Genetic counselling, a form of primary prevention, is described as an attempt to determine which of the following?
options: The risk of occurrence or reoccurrence of specific genetic or chromosomal disorders
The exact IQ the unborn child will have

stem: What is the purpose of genetic counselling in terms of parental decision-making?
options: To allow parents to make an informed choice regarding the risk of having a retarded child
To mandate termination of all high-risk pregnancies
To remove the need for any further antenatal care
To guarantee a gifted child will be born

stem: Which immunization is specifically listed as a form of primary prevention of handicap?
options: Immunization against tetanus in adolescents only
Immunization against poliomyelitis in adulthood only

stem: Adequate maternal nutrition, as a primary prevention measure, is said to lay a foundation for which of the following?
options: A sound metabolic foundation for later child-bearing
An immediate increase in the mother's own IQ
A guaranteed reduction in labour duration
A permanent cure for existing handicaps

stem: Family planning, as a primary prevention measure, can affect specific causal agents through which factors?
options: Size, appropriate spacing, and age of parents
The family's choice of school for existing children

stem: Secondary prevention of handicap involves early detection and treatment of which type of disorders?
options: Preventable disorders such as phenylketonuria and hypothyroidism
Only disorders that are already irreversible

stem: Phenylketonuria and hypothyroidism, if detected early, can be effectively treated at an early stage using which approach?
options: Dietary control and hormone replacement therapy
No treatment is possible even with early detection

stem: Early detection of the presence of mental retardation is important because a delay in diagnosis may cause which outcome?
options: An automatic improvement in the child's IQ
A guaranteed cure without further intervention
No measurable effect on the child's development

stem: Psychiatric treatment, under secondary prevention, is primarily aimed at addressing which difficulties?
options: Only communication difficulties arising from deafness

stem: Tertiary prevention of handicap involves rehabilitation in which areas?
Rehabilitation under tertiary prevention is aimed at achieving which outcome for a child with mental retardation?
options: Reducing disability and providing optimal functioning
Eliminating the need for any further assessment
Guaranteeing admission to a mainstream university

stem: What is the standard formula used to calculate Intelligence Quotient (IQ)?
options: Mental age multiplied by 100, divided by real (chronological) age
Real age multiplied by 100, divided by mental age
Mental age divided by 100, multiplied by real age
Real age minus mental age, multiplied by 100

stem: A child aged 10 years has a mental age of 12 years. Using the standard IQ formula, what is this child's IQ?
According to the IQ formula and classification given, what IQ percentage should a NORMAL child have?
A gifted child, according to the classification given, could have an IQ of what value or higher?
An IQ of between 120 and 125 corresponds to which classification?
An IQ of between 115 and 120 corresponds to which classification?
An IQ of between 90 and 115 corresponds to which classification?
An IQ of between 80 and 90 corresponds to which classification?
An IQ of between 55 and 90 corresponds to which classification, according to the ranges given?
An IQ of less than 50 corresponds to which classification?
Which of the following is listed as a type of handicap?
Besides locomotive handicap, which of the following are ALSO listed as types of handicap?
options: Communication, visual, intellectual, emotional, social, visceral, and invisible handicap

stem: The management of an exceptional child DIFFERS depending on which factor?
options: Whether the child is gifted or handicapped
The child's favourite subject in school
The time of year the child was born
The child's birth order within the family

stem: For gifted children, what type of recognition is given to this group both nationally and internationally?
options: Special performance awards such as scholarships
Mandatory enrolment in vocational training only
Referral to special care centres only
No recognition is given at any level

stem: Scholarships awarded to gifted children serve what specific purpose?
options: To enable them to face the right challenge that is commensurate with their IQ level
To cover only the cost of school uniforms
To replace the need for any further assessment

stem: For handicapped children, careful assessment of their potentials is done for what purpose?
options: To know where to fix them, either to refer them to special care centres for advice or to proper rehabilitation centres
To determine their eligibility for international scholarships only
To rank them against gifted children
To decide whether they should repeat a school grade only

stem: Which of the following is listed as a main element in the comprehensive service for mentally retarded individuals and their families?
options: Prevention and early detection of mental handicaps
Only financial compensation for the family
Only long-term hospitalization with no community involvement

stem: Which element of the comprehensive service specifically addresses the needs of families of mentally retarded individuals?
options: Advice, support, and practical measures for families
Mandatory removal of the child from the family home
Financial penalties for families who seek support
Exclusion of families from all care planning

stem: Which element of the comprehensive service addresses education and occupation for the handicapped person?
options: Provision for education, training, occupation, or work appropriate for each handicapped person
Guaranteed employment in any field regardless of ability
Education limited strictly to religious instruction

stem: Which element of the comprehensive service addresses living arrangements and self-care?
options: Housing and social support to enable self care
Permanent institutionalization with no self-care goals
Housing provided only to families, never to the individual
No housing provision is included in the comprehensive service

stem: Which element of the comprehensive service covers medical and nursing needs across different care settings?
options: Medical, nursing, and other services for those who require them as outpatients, day patients, or inpatients
Medical services provided only to inpatients, never outpatients
Nursing services excluded entirely from the comprehensive service
Medical services limited strictly to emergency care

stem: Which element of the comprehensive service addresses the mental health needs of the mentally retarded individual?
Besides the main elements already listed, general provision for handicapped individuals ALSO includes which of the following?
options: Vocational training, parent counselling, and nursing management
Only annual medical check-ups with no other service

stem: Among the care and rehabilitative measures listed, which pairing BEST reflects two measures mentioned together?
options: Permanent isolation and denial of education
Financial penalty and exclusion from healthcare
Mandatory relocation and loss of citizenship

stem: Which TWO measures, listed together among the care and rehabilitative measures, combine treatment with teaching?
options: Vocational training and housing provision only
Family planning and dietary control only

stem: Which TWO measures, listed together among the care and rehabilitative measures, relate to work and occupation?
options: Vocational training and provision of employment
Centre for guidance and counselling only

stem: Which TWO measures, listed together among the care and rehabilitative measures, focus on guidance and family involvement?
options: Centre for guidance and counselling, and counselling handicapped persons and their parents or family
Provision of employment and designing special gadgets only
Genetic counselling and family planning only

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A 9-year-old child is found on testing to have a mental age of 7.2 years. Using the standard IQ formula, which classification BEST fits this child, and what underlying cause category should the nurse consider exploring FIRST in the child's history?
options: An IQ of 80% places the child at the boundary of a retarded school child; the nurse should first explore both congenital/hereditary and acquired (prenatal, perinatal, postnatal) causes in the history
An IQ of 80% automatically confirms Down syndrome regardless of other findings
An IQ of 80% indicates the child is gifted and requires only a scholarship referral
An IQ of 80% is clinically meaningless and requires no further history-taking

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A mother who took an unspecified drug during the first trimester of pregnancy delivers a child later found to have a limb abnormality, with no family history of similar conditions and no chromosomal abnormality on testing. Which category of cause is MOST consistent with this presentation?
options: A prenatal (environmental) cause, similar to the known effect of thalidomide taken during the first trimester
A postnatal cause, since the exposure occurred during pregnancy rather than after birth
A perinatal/natal cause, since the abnormality was identified at the time of delivery
A purely congenital/genetic cause, since no environmental exposure can produce limb abnormalities

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A neonate experiences a prolonged difficult delivery complicated by cord prolapse, followed by documented hypoglycemia and respiratory acidosis in the first hours of life. The family asks the nurse which prevention strategy would have been relevant BEFORE this pregnancy, versus which is relevant NOW. Which response is MOST accurate?
options: Genetic counselling and adequate maternal nutrition are primary prevention measures relevant before and during pregnancy; early detection and rehabilitation now fall under secondary and tertiary prevention
Genetic counselling is irrelevant to this case because the causes were entirely perinatal, not genetic
Only tertiary prevention measures exist for any case involving perinatal complications
Immunization for maternal rubella would have fully prevented the cord prolapse and hypoglycemia

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A child with a diagnosed mobility impairment that limits independent movement, but with normal intellectual and social functioning, is being classified by the community health team. Which type of handicap BEST describes this child, and how does it differ from a child with an intellectual handicap?
options: A locomotive handicap, which affects mobility specifically, in contrast to an intellectual handicap, which affects cognitive and learning capacity
A visceral handicap, since all handicaps affecting the body are classified as visceral
An invisible handicap, since mobility impairments are never visible to others
A communication handicap, since all physical impairments are classified under communication

stem: CASE SCENARIO: Two children are being discussed at a community health planning meeting: one has an IQ of 122 and excels academically, the other has an IQ of 45 and requires significant support with daily activities. Which pairing of management approaches is MOST appropriate for each child respectively?
options: The first child should be considered for scholarships and tasks commensurate with her IQ level; the second child requires careful assessment of potentials and referral to special care or rehabilitation centres
Both children should receive identical scholarship awards regardless of their differing needs
The first child should be referred to a rehabilitation centre, while the second child should receive a scholarship
Neither child requires any further assessment once their IQ has been documented
